Imagery leads. Yardage supports.

You were right: the promo page drifted into a data sheet. Every image on it is a product cutout, and the Yardage details ended up carrying the personality. This is the fix: same colours, same type, but photography does the talking and the instruments only show up where there's a real number.

The rules

1 · Every page opens on a photoA full-bleed shot of the club (or a person) in the real world, headline over it. Never a grid of cutouts first.
2 · A photo band every two sectionsThe page breathes on photography, not on colour. Two content sections in a row, then a band of real shots.
3 · Cutouts are for choosingStudio cutouts live on cards and pickers. Photos are for wanting. Both, never one without the other.
4 · Yardage only on real numbersThe progress bar and the tracer. No contour wallpaper, no rulers as decoration.
5 · Gold is metal firstThe gold should come from the clubs in the photos. The gradient is for prices and one button.
6 · Real people, our gearNo competitor logos on anyone. A person in a Nike polo never goes big. That's the biggest gap to shoot.

Two grounds, one rhythm

The green was too much because nothing broke it up. Same with white: it only reads as a wireframe without photos. With the photo rhythm, either ground works.
